significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would license the form-(iii) conclusion that cross-lingual factual interference "decays with typological and script distance" and is directionally stronger from high-resource languages, together with the form-(ii) mechanism that a "compact set of shared concept-binding neurons" causally carries that interference and can be manipulated while preserving legitimate transfer. This fixes expectations for untested language pairs and predicts collateral effects of multilingual knowledge editing; ECLeKTic (Hu et al., 2024) and the ROME/MEMIT editing line make such transfer and editing behavior consequential objects of current evaluation rather than merely descriptive representations. It establishes both a broad behavioral phenomenon and a causal mechanism; verified false is also informative because it rules out the distance-graded, resource-asymmetric, compact-neuron account, although the bundled subclaims could fail separately. True and false are distinguishable through the stated ordering and mediation claims, and the topic-substitution check lowers a generic shared-versus-specific representation hypothesis to about 5, so the higher score comes specifically from this predictive law and linked mechanism.

reach.justification: The claim names several usable handles: a "quantitative interference-vs-distance model," an "N-language x N-language directional interference matrix," identified "interference-carrying neurons," and a "training-free intervention that reduces harmful spillover." The distance model is ex ante because it can forecast which target languages are most vulnerable before a fact is injected or edited, while the neuron intervention provides a deployment or editing control rather than only a post-hoc explanation. After model-specific re-extraction, the asserted close-greater-than-distant ordering and source-resource asymmetry still predict what should be found across multilingual model families and language pairs, so more than a search procedure transfers; likely downstream users include knowledge-editing researchers and practitioners auditing or gating multilingual updates. Under topic substitution, generic multilingual representation research would not supply these forecasting and mitigation handles and would merit only the topic-median reach, so the score reflects the claim-specific relation and action window.
